questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road is getting wider.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is coming up.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: Before you change lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one is there.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol naturally.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol naturally.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your body.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing the street in a crosswalk. You must:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn them.
Slow down and carefully drive around them.
Stop and wait until they finish crossing.
Speed up once they pass your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until they finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks. You must always yield to them. Never make a pedestrian wait for your vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving an unfamiliar car that belongs to a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry because all cars are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how to use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how to use them.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, take time to locate and understand the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you start driving.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower thinking and reaction time.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol harm your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: You hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you. You should:

options.text: Stop right where you are.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see emergency lights behind you, slow down and pull safely to the right side of the road. Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: On a freeway, you miss your exit. You should:

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until the next safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway. Instead, continue to the next exit or safe location where you can turn around safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging from the side.
Multiple turns ahead.
The lanes are shifting.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the side.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic will be merging from the right. Get ready to allow that traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light signals.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When an officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light. Officers can tell you to do things differently than what the signals show.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let other cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road, if cars are backing up behind you, pull over and let them pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait for a safe gap and merge carefully.

questions.question: In a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you enter the wrong freeway ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you reach a safe place to pull off. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
A stop sign is posted.
Flashing red lights and gates are on and working.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when told by a flagger, when a stop sign is posted, or when flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: When turning right from a two-way street onto another two-way street, you should:

options.text: Signal your turn for at least 100 feet.
Watch out the right side of the windshield for pedestrians.
Move into the right lane well before the turn.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: When turning right from a two-way street, move into the right lane early and signal your turn in advance. Watch for pedestrians crossing the street by looking out the right side of your windshield.

questions.question: The best safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
questions.explanation: Safety belts greatly increase your chances of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with safety belts in a front-end crash. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to hazards. To avoid highway fatigue, do not stare at one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: This road sign indicates:

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended maximum safe speed for a highway exit. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.
